note: BLM (Colorado River Valley FO) campground on the Eagle River just off I-70 Exit 140 at Gypsum: turn south, then right on the frontage road (Old Highway 6) 1.5 miles past the roundabout. Gravel loops between the interstate and the river; a trail leads to the river for fishing and raft access (floating late May-July). Reviewers fit 24-30 ft rigs; the sites further up the road are the better ones. Constant I-70 noise. --Claude
summary: BLM page: confirmed open May 15 - Nov 15, first-come only (no reservations), $20/night, phone (970) 876-9000. Cleared site count 8, max 30 ft and vault toilets - none is stated by BLM or recreation.gov (listings/reviews only). Not waterfront stands. Pin on the west loop. Note trimmed.
flags: No agency site count, length limit or amenity list: the BLM page gives only season, FCFS and fee; recreation.gov 261760 is a point of interest with no campsite catalog. Cleared the listing-derived count (8), max_rig_ft (30) and vault_toilets. No 'small RV' wording; camper reviews report 24-30 ft rigs.

Wording: BLM says the campground 'offers gravel roads with primitive walk in fishing and camping' - imagery shows two drive-in gravel loops with back-in spurs and parked RVs, so read as drive-in; noting it in case the human reads it otherwise.
Phone 970-876-9000 confirmed (Colorado River Valley Field Office, BLM page).

Waterfront (stored not waterfront) stands: the Eagle River (~30-40 m wide) runs ~60-150 m south of the loops behind a continuous belt of riparian woods and willow; the loops sit between the river thicket and I-70.
Pin 39.65455,-106.9764 is at the south end of the west loop; recreation.gov point 39.65555,-106.9762 is the entrance off the frontage road (~110 m north). OK.
